# Macro recovery and synthetic-local references

These complete Joern 4.0.555 graphs pin recovery when an unresolved token between string literals invalidates a macro-expanded call argument. Block declarations recover their original source without macro or expression name resolution. Joern drops invalid standalone call statements, retains UNKNOWN returns, and wraps invalid conditions in a comparison with zero. Lexical binding state survives shadowing and does not leak into later methods. Recovered identifiers retain their types while displaying unresolved CODE, including when the macro argument matcher considers them.

The same pinned VariableScopeManager prepends pending references: the last identifier reference determines synthetic-local order and CODE. Direct callees and METHOD_REF nodes do not participate. The fixtures include ordinary/repeated unknowns, globals, function values, NULL and sizeof. C2's sizeof lowering uses the declaration specifier without pointer, array or function declarators; primitive qualifiers remain in CODE, while NAME and TYPE keep their separately measured spelling.

48 complete graphs are asserted. Four complete diagnostics retain unsupported bare string/array initializer recovery, malformed for-initializer fragments, and typedef-name disambiguation in sizeof(Alias). No canonical records are filtered. Both complete raw scripts/outputs and every input/reference/baseline/candidate are bound by measurement.json. Counts include empty method separators only where explicitly labelled. Historical failed implementation probes are retained in .local/astra-sprint/fifth-batch/g-write. These graphs cover the selected canonical projection, not all Joern schema fields or product behavior.
